chief_complaint: widespread hives, wheezing, and lightheadedness post-sting
hpi_details: A 44-year-old female presents to the clinic with widespread hives, wheezing, and lightheadedness post-sting. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
ideas: She thinks the wasp that stung her was an unusually poisonous species with dangerous venom.
concerns: She is terrified that she might pass out and collapse on the floor while she is home alone caring for her young daughter.
expectations: She hopes to receive immediate treatment to stop the dizziness and a prescription for an emergency shot pen to keep with her.

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Anaphylaxis (wasp sting-triggered) is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management emphasizes immediate intramuscular epinephrine (0.3–0.5 mg for most adults), emergency monitoring, and supportive care, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Anaphylaxis (wasp sting-triggered).
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Large local sting reaction (no systemic symptoms) without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Wheeze or lightheadedness — this is systemic, not just a local reaction.
management_principles: Plan for Wasp Sting Anaphylaxis: Immediate intramuscular epinephrine (0.3–0.5 mg for most adults), emergency monitoring, and IV fluids when indicated
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

teaching.one_liner: A systemic IgE-mediated reaction to insect venom with hives, wheeze, and lightheadedness after a sting — treated immediately with intramuscular epinephrine.
differentials: Large local sting reaction (no systemic symptoms)
red_flags: Wheeze or lightheadedness — this is systemic, not just a local reaction

must_ask.say: Where were you stung, and how soon after did symptoms start?
Are the hives all over your body, or just around the sting site?
Do you feel wheezy, short of breath, or lightheaded?
Have you ever reacted this way to a sting before?
Do you carry epinephrine, and has it been given?

history.answer: I was stung by a wasp about thirty minutes ago, and now I'm breaking out in itchy hives all over, my chest feels tight and wheezy, and I feel really dizzy.
It started about twenty to thirty minutes ago right after I was stung on my arm, and the red bumps quickly spread all across my chest, belly, and legs.
The rash covers my entire chest, stomach, back, arms, and thighs, as well as parts of my face and neck.
They look like raised, swollen red welts of different shapes and sizes that turn white when I press on them, with no blisters or scabs.
It is intensely itchy all over my body, but there is no burning pain or numbness.
New ones keep popping up and merging together continuously since the sting; none of them have faded away yet.
My lips and eyelids feel a bit puffy, and my throat feels tight, like I have a lump I can't swallow away.
Yes, I am short of breath and I can hear a high-pitched whistling sound whenever I breathe out.
I felt a sudden wave of dizziness and lightheadedness when I stood up, and I feel faint and weak.
I was stung once on my right forearm by a yellow-and-black wasp while trimming shrubs in my backyard about half an hour ago; the stinger didn't stay in.
I was stung once a couple of years ago, but it only caused a quarter-sized red swelling on my hand that cleared up in a day.
No, I have never had an allergic reaction like this before, so I do not have an epinephrine auto-injector and haven't used any medicine today.
I don't have chills or a fever, but I feel overwhelmingly weak, exhausted, and shaky all over.
No, I don't have any sores, blisters, or raw peeling areas inside my mouth, eyes, or private areas.
No, my skin is not peeling off or tender to the touch, and there are no purple spots that stay purple when pressed.
No, I haven't started any new antibiotics, pain relievers, gout pills, or seizure medications recently.
No, I haven't eaten any unusual seafood, nuts, or new foods today; I just had my usual toast and coffee this morning.
No new cosmetics, body lotions, laundry detergents, or new jewelry; I was only exposed to the outdoor garden shrubs.
No travel, no hiking in deep woods, and no visits to public spas or gyms; just my own backyard.
No one else at home has any rash, itching, or similar symptoms.
No, I don't have a history of asthma, eczema, or severe allergic rhinitis.
No, my joints are not painful or swollen, and my nails look completely normal.
I washed the sting site with tap water right away, but I haven't put any hydrocortisone cream or antifungal ointment on it.
I have been in a monogamous relationship with my husband for twenty years, and I have no history of genital sores or sexually transmitted infections.
I thought maybe that specific wasp was extra poisonous, because I've never had a bug bite make me feel faint before.
I'm really scared that I'll faint and collapse while my little girl is alone with me at home.
I hope you can give me something right away to keep me from blacking out, and prescribe an emergency pen I can carry in my bag.
I have been generally healthy with no chronic medical conditions like diabetes, hypertension, or heart disease.
I have never had any surgeries and have never been hospitalized except when I gave birth to my children.
I do not take any prescription medications, over-the-counter painkillers, or herbal supplements.
I have no known allergies to medications, foods, or latex.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used any tobacco or vaping products.
I only drink a glass of wine socially once or twice a month, and none today.
I work as an administrative assistant at an accounting firm and live with my husband and two teenage children.
There is no family history of severe allergies, asthma, autoimmune skin conditions, or sudden unexplained collapse.
My last menstrual period started twelve days ago and was normal; my cycles are regular, my husband had a vasectomy, and there is no chance I am pregnant.

exam.finding: The patient appears acutely distressed, diaphoretic, and anxious, with labored breathing and prominent widespread erythema.
Blood pressure 90/60 mmHg, heart rate 112 beats/min, respiratory rate 24 breaths/min, SpO2 94% on ambient air, temperature 36.8°C.
Widespread erythematous, raised, edematous wheals with central pallor across trunk, limbs, and face; single puncture mark on right forearm with surrounding erythema.
Bilateral mild conjunctival hyperemia without purulent discharge, petechiae, or scleral icterus.
Mild edema of the uvula and posterior pharyngeal wall without gross airway occlusion; tongue and oral mucosa are moist with no ulcers.
No enlarged, tender, or palpable cervical or supraclavicular lymph nodes.
Diffuse bilateral expiratory high-pitched wheezes with mildly prolonged expiratory phase; no inspiratory stridor or basal crackles.
Tachycardic regular rhythm, crisp S1 and S2, without murmurs, third heart sound, or friction rubs.
Radial and dorsalis pedis pulses are rapid, equal, and mildly thready.
Abdomen is soft, non-distended, and non-tender throughout, with normal active bowel sounds and no rebound tenderness.
No pitting edema of the lower extremities; peripheral extremities are warm with capillary refill time under two seconds.
